findings.description: Switching the match handling from truthiness to `is not None` means an empty-string match pattern is now compiled instead of being rejected as missing, and `re.compile("").match` succeeds on any string.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a caller passes match="" with message omitted. Before the change, the falsy check raised TypeError ('missing 1 required argument'). Now match="" is compiled to an empty pattern, so _check returns True for every exception. Impact: the predicate silently retries on all exceptions, including ones the caller meant to exclude, instead of failing fast at construction.
